# Doctor: mapping-config diagnostics with offline-always / live-drift-degrades portability

## Context / Problem

The mapping seam (S1–S8) adds a hand-editable `[mapping]` config surface. Two failure classes
need surfacing before a reconcile drifts silently:

- **Internally-invalid config** — already fail-closed via `MappingConfigError` (a `ConfigError`
  subclass): a non-integer `hierarchy` rank / malformed block fail at LOAD; an
  out-of-vocabulary axis value and an unmapped-non-skipped type fail in the
  `rebar_reconciler.config` resolvers. Doctor should surface these as **error** findings.
- **Live drift** — internally valid but disagreeing with live Jira (a mapped status/type/link
  Jira no longer exposes). Surface when Jira is reachable; degrade cleanly when not.

`rebar doctor` is the existing diagnostic home, so extend it, not a new command. It must stay
portable: it runs where the optional **`jira-datacenter`** extra is absent and no credentials
are set. Offline checks always run; the live-drift check degrades to an `unavailable` finding,
mirroring `rebar metrics`'s `unavailable` (`docs/user-guide.md`).

## Approach

Add a mapping-diagnostics function to `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`, wired into `scan`/the
doctor CLI. Mapping findings go in their **own list** (as doctor does for scan-dirty/lock reports), are rendered and folded into the exit code, and kept **out of** `run_repair`'s
iteration — so `doctor.scan()`'s blocking-edge finding contract (and `run_repair` /
`repair_finding` / `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`) is unchanged.

- **Offline checks (always run, stdlib-only, no Jira import):** run the provider-neutral
  `rebar_reconciler.config` resolvers — `effective_status_map`, `effective_type_map`,
  `assert_type_decisions_complete`, `effective_link_map` — against the loaded config. Load the
  `MappingConfig` once, then enumerate every configured key in `config.projects` **union the
  default layer**, running the resolvers per key so per-project errors are actually reached and
  named. The resolvers inject the built-in `MappingLayer` (`local_to_jira_status` /
  `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` / link literal) + `Capability`, import `mapping_config` lazily, and are
  stdlib-only at import (never `adapters.jira*`). Any `MappingConfigError` (non-integer
  hierarchy, malformed block, out-of-vocabulary status/type/link value, unmapped-non-skipped
  type) → an **error** finding naming the key (non-zero exit). Additionally, on the same per-key
  pass, report one genuinely *soft* problem that is NOT a load error — an all-empty
  `projects.<KEY>` block (likely stub) — as a **warning** naming the key.
- **Live-drift check (best-effort, degrades):** run only when the `jira-datacenter` extra is
  importable — gated through `rebar._optional.capability_installed("jira_datacenter")` — AND
  credentials resolve. On the available path, reuse S8's read-only probe reader
  (`mapping_probe.build_probe`, backed by `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings`) and diff the
  configured vocabulary against observed Jira vocabulary, one finding per divergence on the axes
  the reader observes: **status, type, link** (a configured value absent from Jira's set).
  Hierarchy is deliberately **excluded** from the live diff: `build_probe` resolves Data Center,
  and `mapping_probe._hierarchy` documents `hierarchyLevel` as Cloud-only — on Data Center it is
  always empty and `hierarchy` is dropped, so a hierarchy divergence is structurally
  undetectable via this reader (offline hierarchy validity is still covered above). When the
  extra is absent, OR the resolved PAT is empty (`JIRA_PAT` unset —
  `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` is total, returning `pat=""`), OR settings resolution
  raises `ConfigError` (it fails loud on a malformed `[tool.rebar.reconciler]`), OR the probe
  transport raises or times out (the probe runs under a bounded timeout — S8's `build_probe`
  transport, or wrapped here — so a slow/hanging Data Center host degrades not blocks),
  emit a single `unavailable` finding ("live mapping-drift check skipped: <reason>") and return
  success — never raise. The Jira import and settings/probe construction
  happen lazily inside the check, behind the guard and wrapped so every degradation cause folds
  into the one `unavailable` finding.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` — new mapping-diagnostics function (own findings list); the
  `capability_installed("jira_datacenter")` guard and lazy Jira import.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — document the offline error/warning findings and the `unavailable`
  live-drift convention.
- Reuses S1's `mapping_config` via the `rebar_reconciler.config` resolvers and S8's
  `mapping_probe.build_probe`; adds no config surface.
- Out of scope: `--repair` auto-fixing mapping config (report-only); Jira as a hard doctor
  dependency; the live-drift **true path against real Jira** — E2E transport is S8's proven
  read-only probe reader (covered by S8's tests), so this child proves the diff logic through an
  injected vocabulary and treats the real-transport path as explicitly not-applicable.

## Testing

- **Unit (offline tier), no Jira import:** temp config with (a) valid mapping → no findings;
  (b) each error-class problem (non-integer hierarchy, out-of-vocabulary value,
  unmapped-non-skipped type) → an **error** finding naming the key + non-zero exit; (c) an
  all-empty `projects.<KEY>` block → a **warning** finding naming the key. Asserts no
  `adapters.jira` import on this path. Oracle: finding list + exit code.
- **Unit (portability tier):** force the guard false (monkeypatch `capability_installed` for
  `"jira_datacenter"`) → exactly one `unavailable` finding, success exit, no Jira import. Oracle:
  the single finding + zero exit.
- **Unit (degradation causes):** guard true; drive each non-transport cause — empty resolved
  PAT, and a `ConfigError` from settings resolution — each folds into one `unavailable` finding
  with the matching reason + success exit. Oracle: the finding + reason + zero exit.
- **Unit (live-drift tier), injected transport:** inject a fake probe reader whose vocabulary
  diverges on status, type, and link → one drift finding per divergence naming the axis and
  absent value. No live Jira. Oracle: the per-axis finding set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar doctor` on a valid `[mapping]` config with the `jira-datacenter` extra absent
  succeeds and emits exactly one `unavailable` live-drift finding — portability-tier test (guard
  forced false via `capability_installed`, no Jira import, zero exit).
- [ ] Each offline error-class problem (non-integer hierarchy, out-of-vocabulary value,
  unmapped-non-skipped type) yields an **error** finding naming the key + non-zero exit — the
  offline check enumerates `config.projects` + the default layer per key; offline-tier test
  running the `rebar_reconciler.config` resolvers and asserting the
  `MappingConfigError`-derived finding.
- [ ] An all-empty `projects.<KEY>` stub yields a **warning** finding naming the key (not an
  error, not a non-zero exit) — offline-tier test.
- [ ] Each non-transport degradation cause — extra absent, empty resolved PAT (`JIRA_PAT`
  unset), and a `ConfigError` from settings resolution — folds into a single `unavailable`
  finding + reason + success exit — portability and degradation-cause tests.
- [ ] With a fake probe reader injected, each configured-vs-observed divergence on status, type,
  and link yields a drift finding naming the axis and absent value — live-drift-tier test.
  (Hierarchy is excluded by design: the reused Data Center probe never observes
  `hierarchyLevel`.)
- [ ] The doctor module imports and `rebar doctor` runs with the `jira-datacenter` extra
  uninstalled — portability-tier test asserting the Jira import is lazy/guarded.
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` documents the new mapping diagnostics.

All four test tiers run in-process with no live Jira and no specific CI provider, satisfying
`project.portability`.
